page.overview:
What is Pichu?

Pichu are very small, plump, yellow rodent-like Pokémon. It bares a similar appearance to its evolved form Pikachu, but varies in a number of ways. Pichu have diamond-shaped ears on the top of their head, with the edges being black and the interior yellow. Underneath their head is a black pattern, that somewhat resembles a collar. Their tails are completely black, and resemble a small lightning bolt, similar to its evolved forms, which are larger. Pichu also have round, pink sacs on their cheeks, used for storing electricity.

A Shiny Pichu has its fur being darker and matches that of Pikachu.

Pichu, like its other forms, is capable of storing electricity in the pink sacs on its cheeks, and is strong enough to zap an adult human. Being a baby Pokémon, however, it is not proficient at controlling its powers and cannot store as much electricity as its evolved forms; Pichu will shock itself if any electrical energy leaks out of its cheeks, even when attacking in battle or defending its Trainer from harm (does not occur in gameplay). It can even shoot out sparks if startled or excited. Despite this, it does learn over time and tends to be better in stormy weather or at dry areas.

Pichu are usually playful and happy Pokémon, though some can be mischievous, as seen in the cases of the Pichu Brothers in some older media. When playing with its own kind, they short out their power, which can lead it to cry and startle itself.
